solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Said of country life all but past

indicators.note: all but past tells us to keep everything except the word past from the longer word

parts.note: pastoral means relating to rural, country life
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A remark about rural living that has nearly all faded into history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but past' looks like 'almost past', but it means remove PAST from PASTORAL, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes something spoken rather than written, so it is a synonym of said.

clue.text: Famous Belgian showing determination in match

indicators.note: in places the word for determination inside the word for match

parts.note: to match is to mate, pair up
grit is courage and resolve

explanation.surface: A celebrated Belgian displays resolve during a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting contest, but here it means to mate or pair.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a celebrated Belgian surrealist painter.

clue.text: Doctor caught in high wind might mean to take a chance

indicators.note: caught in means held within the word for a high wind

parts.note: a gale is a very strong wind
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Being stuck in a storm with a physician might make you take a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To gamble is to risk something on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: To keep mum quiet, work or cease trading?

parts.note: to keep quiet, say nothing, is to shut up
shop means one's work or business, as in talking shop

explanation.surface: A question asking whether silencing your mother is a job or a way to close a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother but means silent; 'shop' as in 'talk shop' means one's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Shutting up shop is an idiom for closing a business, or stopping work for the day.

clue.text: Inactive rook, chess piece put in spot

indicators.note: put in places the rook and the piece inside the word for spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
a man is any chess piece

explanation.surface: A chess note about an idle rook and another piece being placed on a square.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant describes something asleep or inactive for now, like a volcano.

clue.text: Benefactor's name in entrance

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A benefactor's name is displayed at the entrance of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods, which is what a benefactor does.

clue.text: Country doctor taken up, about to ring a bird of prey

parts.note: Turkey is a country
to buzz someone is to give them a ring on the phone

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A rural doctor, lifted up and about to phone, is likened to a hunting bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken up' reads the doctor upwards in this down entry; 'about' is a loose link letting that piece come round to the end of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey buzzard, or turkey vulture, is an American carrion-eating raptor.

clue.text: Plug Rhine wine, mostly for this special purpose

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, shortened to ad

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: An instruction to promote a German white wine, mostly for this one occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like a stopper for the wine bottle, but it is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this', meaning made for one particular purpose.

clue.text: Almost heaven, after tea, this French wine

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word following the word for tea

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: bliss is a heavenly state of happiness

explanation.surface: Nearly heavenly after a cup of tea: this French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from Burgundy in France.

clue.text: Fisherman's position by river

parts.note: an angle is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: A fisherman takes up a spot on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; 'by' just puts the river after the position.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is someone who fishes with rod and line.

clue.text: Scapegoat in genuine denial

indicators.note: in places the word for scapegoat inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
a butt is the target of blame or jokes

explanation.surface: Someone made a scapegoat issues a sincere denial.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation or contradiction of a claim.

clue.text: Enlisted man to see detective

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A soldier goes to see a sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is an informal term for a private investigator.

clue.text: Shower before party game

indicators.note: before places the shower word ahead of the party word

parts.note: a volley is a shower of missiles
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: Freshen up before a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' looks like washing, but a volley is a shower of shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Volleyball is a team sport played by hitting a ball over a high net.

clue.text: Hide in shower

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with the fur on
to rain down hard or bombard with things

explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal skin, and to pelt is to shower with missiles or rain.

clue.text: Season's first evil winds — onset of ripsnorter lashes trees

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word season's
winds means the letters of evil are twisted into a new order
onset of means take the opening letter of ripsnorter

parts.note: to birch someone is to lash or flog them

explanation.surface: A storm opens the season, its fierce winds lashing the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver birches are slender trees with white peeling bark.

clue.text: Not quite certain matter involves large balance

indicators.note: not quite means the word is missing its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: involves means the word for matter takes in the abbreviation for large

parts.note: pus is matter discharged by an infection

explanation.surface: Uncertain about a matter that involves a large balance in an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like 'issue', but it is the medical sense, pus.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount left over, like a positive balance on an account.

clue.text: Cavalier sort stupidly accepting one bet retrospectively

indicators.note: accepting means the shuffled letters take in the turned piece
stupidly says the letters of sort are jumbled
retrospectively means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to lay is to place a bet

explanation.surface: A carefree type foolishly accepting a wager made in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupidly' makes ROST from SORT, which takes in YALI (I LAY reversed by 'retrospectively').
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers were the supporters of King Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: King in charge, not bound by rules

indicators.note: in places the king's letter inside the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king in power is above the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free means being unrestricted, not held to any constraint.

clue.text: Gillespie's turn?

parts.note: Dizzy Gillespie was a jazz trumpeter, and his turn or spell could be named after his nickname

explanation.definitionFit: A dizzy spell is a bout of giddiness, punned on jazz trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie.

clue.text: Cattle dealer bringing third of herd into port

indicators.note: into places the chosen letter inside the port

parts.note: Dover is a port on the English Channel coast

indicators.note: third of means take the third letter of herd

explanation.surface: A cattleman brings a portion of his herd into a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover drives herds of livestock to market, and some also traded them.

clue.text: Hungarian pianist making record that must be heard

indicators.note: must be heard says the word for record is to be taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A Hungarian performer cuts a record that people should listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a celebrated nineteenth-century Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Drink in nightspots a party knocked back

parts.note: clubs are nightspots for dancing

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Drinking at nightclubs where a party drink is downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses A DO into ODA.
explanation.definitionFit: Club soda is carbonated water used as a mixer.

clue.text: Insect found in place close to rainforest

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of rainforest

explanation.surface: A bug discovered somewhere near a tropical forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a swarming grasshopper.

clue.text: Revolutionary female cook

parts.note: Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebellious woman who cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook.

clue.text: Work out volume in one

indicators.note: in places the volume abbreviation inside the word for one

parts.note: sole means single or one only

explanation.surface: Calculate the amount in a single container.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to work out its answer.

clue.text: Opposition leader in Duma is told to go

indicators.note: leader in means take the opening letter of Duma

parts.note: taken as written
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: The head of the Russian parliament is ordered to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duma is the Russian parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement or opposition to an official view.
